Hardening on top of `v0.1.0-alpha.1`. A deployment can now define its own
operator account, the web interface has been rebuilt, and both the CLI and the
server can say which version they are running and whether a newer one exists.

Still an **alpha**. Nothing here is a stability promise.

## Highlights

**A deployment can define its own operator.** `CAIRN_ADMIN_EMAIL` and
`CAIRN_ADMIN_PASSWORD` create the account a fresh server signs in with, applied
after migrations and before the listener binds — so a deployment with unusable
credentials fails to start rather than serving traffic nobody can sign into.
The variables *are* the password, not an initial value: rotating one is an edit
and a restart. Setting only one is a startup error.

**The web interface was rebuilt** on shadcn/ui with a collapsible sidebar
shell, replacing a fixed column whose navigation only existed inside a project.
It brings a breadcrumb, per-route titles, a styled 404, real loading, empty and
error states, and confirmations before anything irreversible.

**API tokens are managed in the browser.** Create, review and revoke personal
tokens from the UI. A new token's plaintext appears exactly once, in a panel
only the reader dismisses, because the server stores a hash and cannot show it
again.

**`cairn update`.** Finds a newer release and installs it, verifying the
archive against the digest the release publishes and refusing on a mismatch.
`cairn` and `cairnd` are replaced together — a half-applied update leaves a CLI
that cannot talk to its own daemon. `cairn update --check` reports without
installing. Prereleases are only offered to someone already running one.

**Knowing what you are running.** `/api/version` reports the deployment's
version, the newest eligible release, and whether it is worth moving to. The
server looks it up once and caches it, so browsers never spend a visitor's
GitHub rate limit. It is shown in the sidebar and on the sign-in page, which is
readable without signing in.

## Security

- **The session cookie is marked `Secure`** when `CAIRN_WEB_ORIGIN` is an
  `https` origin. Deliberately not hardcoded: a browser silently drops a
  `Secure` cookie received in clear, which would break every plain-HTTP
  deployment. The logout cookie carries matching attributes, since a clearing
  cookie that does not match is not guaranteed to clear anything.
- Deleting a memory and revoking a token now ask first. Both are irreversible
  and both sat one stray click away from rows people scan.

## Correctness

- **Stale sessions no longer block the next one.** A `SessionEnd` arriving for
  an agent key the daemon never saw left its session `active` indefinitely, and
  two such sessions in one worktree made `cairn context` fail with
  `ambiguous_session` — the call an agent makes before it knows its own session
  key. Sessions nothing has driven for two hours are now closed with a
  `recovered` handoff.
- **Memory provenance is correct under ambiguity.** Recording a memory
  swallowed every session-resolution error, so ambiguity quietly opened a
  throwaway session and stamped the memory with an origin that never did the
  work. Ambiguity is now the caller's to resolve, and both
  `cairn memory add --session` and the `cairn_remember` MCP tool can name one.
- **Daemons no longer steal a socket that is already being served.** Several
  starting at once replaced each other in turn, and a client connected to a
  displaced daemon saw its connection close mid-request. A daemon stands down
  when someone is already answering, and the CLI retries a handover with
  bounded backoff.

## Also

- `cairn auth status` — whether a credential is stored and for which server.
  The token itself is never printed.
- `cairn daemon logs` — the daemon writes to `cairnd.log` and this reads it.
  Previously `cairn` started it with stderr discarded, so it had no usable log.
- `cairn status` names the server a linked project syncs to, and says when no
  token is stored for it.
- The account menu no longer throws on open; copying a token falls back when
  the async clipboard API is unavailable; the mobile sidebar closes when you
  navigate; memory filters name themselves; memory search is debounced,
  clearable, and reports how many matched.

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Status |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon, `aarch64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| macOS (Intel, `x86_64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| Linux (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Linux (`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Windows | **Not supported** |

Windows support is not implemented: the CLI and daemon communicate over a Unix
domain socket. No Windows artifact is published.

## Upgrading from alpha.1

`cairn update` arrives *in* this release, so alpha.1 has no copy of it. Install
this one over your existing binaries with the steps under **Install** below —
`cairn` and `cairnd` must be replaced together, because they speak a private
protocol to each other. Then restart the daemon:

```bash
cairn daemon stop && cairn daemon start
```

From alpha.2 onward, `cairn update` fetches and replaces both binaries for
you. It does not restart the daemon — it prints the same two commands above,
and you run them.

Your local state is kept. The SQLite store migrates in place, and linked
projects, memory, tasks, sessions and handoffs survive the upgrade, as does the
Claude Code integration.

## Install

Download the archive for your platform, verify it, and put the binaries on your
PATH. `cairn` and `cairnd` must live in the same directory — `cairn` starts the
daemon itself.

```bash
VERSION=0.1.0-alpha.2
TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin   # or x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS

tar -xzf cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairn cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairnd /usr/local/bin/
```

Then, inside a Git repository:

```bash
cairn init
cairn connect claude-code
```

## Container images

Only the server-side components ship as images. The local agent is native by
design.

```
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-server:0.1.0-alpha.2
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-web:0.1.0-alpha.2
```

Both are also published under an immutable `sha-<short-sha>` tag and built for
`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. There is deliberately no `latest` tag for a
pre-release. An example stack is in
[`deploy/docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/blob/main/deploy/docker-compose.yml).

## Verifying what you downloaded

- `SHA256SUMS` covers every archive.
- `SBOM.spdx.json` describes the release contents.
- Archives and images carry GitHub build provenance attestations:

```bash
gh attestation verify cairn-v0.1.0-alpha.2-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz --repo Vellixia/Cairn
```

## Known limitations

- **Alpha.** Expect defects. Do not depend on this for anything you cannot
  reconstruct.
- **Pre-1.0 compatibility.** APIs, storage schemas and the wire protocol may
  change without a deprecation period.
- Sharing requires running your own Cairn server; no hosted service exists.
